title: Verifiability and Interpretability: An Epistemological Framework from the Empirical Paradigm of Deep Learning to the Rational Practice of Artificial General Intelligence
content: Verifiability and interpretability are two dimensions of the epistemic status of an artificial intelligence (AI) system: the former concerns whether outputs and actions can be checked independently of the process that generated them, and the latter whether the decision mechanism can be faithfully understood. Starting from three formulas (verifiable + interpretable = rational practice; verifiable + uninterpretable = empiricism; interpretable + unverifiable = ungrounded theory) and adding a fourth case, the double blind spot, we construct an interpretability–verifiability four-quadrant framework and use it to analyze how the two dimensions are distributed and unbalanced in the pre-training and post-training of large language models, deep reinforcement learning, chain-of-thought reasoning, agent frameworks, embodied intelligence, recursive self-improvement (RSI), and artificial general and super intelligence (AGI/ASI). The analysis indicates the following. Pre-training centered on scaling laws is a form of empiricism: what improves with scale is verifiable prediction error, not interpretable structure or the coverage of verification. Chain-of-thought provides a readable narrative that becomes audit evidence only after its faithfulness has been tested. Reward hacking under finite evaluation is a structural equilibrium of optimized systems. Low-dimensional safety interfaces and certified execution traces allow verifiability to be anchored on narrow interfaces. The bottleneck of RSI lies in the resolution, independence and specification completeness of the verification signal rather than in the generation of candidate improvements. The introspective narratives of intelligent systems are structurally unreliable and should not serve alone as evidence of alignment. On this basis, we propose a risk-stratified decision matrix, an L0–L5 maturity model and a spectrum of interpretability techniques, establish the principle of “verifiability first, interpretability scaled with risk, and the two closed into a complementary loop”, and state testable predictions together with their falsification conditions. This paper is a conceptual analysis based on published evidence.
